minutes.headline: Personnel Committee dropped the two-of-three voting change and began shaping a warrant article on job-description review and a class and comp study.
minutes.summary: The committee discussed two possible warrant articles for town meeting: letting job descriptions with no changes within a set period skip committee review, and funding a town-wide classification and compensation study. After the town's counsel-style clarification on quorum and voting, members agreed to drop the proposal to change the voting threshold. They also planned a SharePoint-based procedures handbook and were reminded not to deliberate in a shared document outside a public meeting. No formal votes other than adjournment were taken.

budget_items.what_was_said: Members said the town would fund a classification and compensation study and that it needs to be approved at town meeting, though bids can be gathered beforehand.

decisions.decision: Members agreed to take the two-of-three voting/quorum change off the list of warrant items.
Action item: email the HR director and town manager about the class and comp study scope and who runs the bidding.
Agreed a workshop with HR on the study's scope would be useful, with requested (not mandatory) attendance.
Chair will put reference documents in SharePoint; members will send questions or markups to the chair individually rather than commenting in a shared document.

what_happened.line: The Personnel Committee agreed to drop the proposal to change the voting and quorum threshold from its list of warrant items.
Members began shaping a warrant article on job-description review, including letting descriptions with no changes within a set period skip committee review.
Members said a town-wide classification and compensation study would need town meeting approval, though bids can be gathered beforehand.
An action item was set to email the HR director and town manager about the study's scope and who runs the bidding; a workshop with HR was also favored.
Members will send questions or markups to the chair individually, not comment in a shared document, to stay within open meeting law.

why_it_matters: A warrant article funding a classification and compensation study would be a town meeting vote residents are asked to take, and it bears on how town jobs are graded and paid.
The job-description change would alter how often committee review happens, which affects how openly changes to town positions get seen.
